answer: A verifiable delay function is a terrace of sequential squaring: the prover squares a seed modulo a 2048-bit modulus 1000000 times, then gives a proof checked in under 10 milliseconds. Parallel machines cannot shorten the chain, just as slow water shapes karst, and a lagoon of extra cores gives no shortcut. An attacker must spend about 12 seconds per identity, so forging 1000 identities costs 3 hours of unavoidable delay.
